primary.thesis: The three-month window runs to 31 Dec 2026, and most listed leaders are safe in it. Scheduled handovers fall after the deadline: Newsom's successor takes office in January 2027, and Brazil's new president is inaugurated in January 2027. Autocrats such as Kim, Xi and Putin rarely leave office for any reason other than death. So if anyone leaves first, it will most likely be someone whose office can be taken away by ordinary procedure. There are three such cases. (1) Lecornu in France: he heads a minority government that has to pass the 2027 budget this autumn in a hung Assembly. He faces censure motions and pressure from parties positioning for the 2027 presidential election. Past French practice (Bayrou fell and Lecornu was named the next day) shows a successor can be appointed within days, which ends the caretaker exception. (2) Netanyahu in Israel: the Knesset election is due around 27 Oct 2026. If an opposition bloc wins and forms a coalition quickly, a new PM could be sworn in before year-end. (3) Delcy Rodríguez in Venezuela: she is only an acting president in a transition managed from outside. Her office can end through a negotiated handover, US pressure or an internal realignment, with no election required. C22 NO covers the remaining cases where someone leaves, such as elderly or fragile incumbents like Abbas, or unexpected coups or deaths.

basket.reason: Lecornu is the most exposed listed leader: minority government, 2027 budget fight, censure motions, and a quick French record of appointing successors, which limits the caretaker exception.
An October 2026 Knesset election gives a real way to replace Netanyahu before year-end if the opposition forms a coalition quickly.
An 'acting' president in an externally managed transition can be replaced by negotiation or pressure, with no electoral calendar needed.
This covers the whole 'someone leaves' outcome, including a death, coup or resignation among the other 18 listed leaders.

failure_narrative: The basket loses only if nobody permanently leaves office by 31 Dec 2026. In that world, Lecornu gets the 2027 budget through, either by Socialists abstaining in exchange for concessions or by a special stop-gap budget law. If he is censured anyway, he stays on as caretaker into January while Macron hunts for a successor. Israel's election gives neither bloc a clear win, or the opposition bloc falls apart in coalition talks. Coalition-building runs past 31 December, and Netanyahu remains caretaker PM, which the rules do not count. Washington treats Rodríguez as its working partner for oil and migration deals, so talk of elections or a handover slips into 2027. No elderly or fragile leader dies or is removed. The result is 'None before 2027'.
hedge_thesis: The failure world has one main thread: Venezuela's transition under Rodríguez becomes a stable arrangement with the US. In that case, US licences and Chevron-led operations raise Venezuelan heavy-sour crude exports to the US Gulf Coast. That extra Venezuelan crude competes directly with Canadian heavy crude for the same Gulf Coast refineries (the ones built to run heavy, sour oil). Alberta producers then face a wider Western Canadian Select discount and weaker netbacks at the Gulf, and Trans Mountain / Asian export routes matter more to them. So the Canadian heavy-oil complex should be under pressure in exactly the worlds where Rodríguez, and with her the status quo, survives. That is Canada rather than Venezuela, and it tends to be true when the primary basket loses.
